intro.name: The trial
intro.text: The judges present one of these questions: What makes a village truly prosperous? Who owns a discovery? Can a promise become unjust? Is courage possible without fear?

choices.label: Invite the whole village to question the answers.

a1.text: An elder gives an elegant speech, but a child's brief answer moves the audience more deeply.

text_only.what: tech, food, or appropriate skill experience
text_only.reason: the trial names no villager to gain skill; this trial's constructive success gives tech

a2.text: A contestant argues that prosperity means full food stores; another points toward the lonely and forgotten. The judges cannot easily choose.

text_only.reason: narrative: an argument about what prosperity means, not a food change

a3.text: The winner admits uncertainty and explains how to test the claim. The scholars praise intellectual humility.

text_only.what: tech, food, or appropriate skill experience
text_only.reason: the trial names no villager to gain skill; this trial's constructive success gives tech

b1.text: The discussion uncovers an unfair village custom, and the council agrees to reconsider it.

text_only.what: tech, food, or appropriate skill experience
text_only.reason: the trial names no villager to gain skill; this trial's constructive success gives tech

b2.text: Every answer creates three more questions. The competition ends at sunset without a winner but with a thriving new study circle.

text_only.what: tech, food, or appropriate skill experience

b3.text: One villager responds with a joke so apt that it becomes a proverb.

p1.text: A judge from the other community praises the winning rival despite pressure from (judge.his/her) own supporters. The crowd slowly applauds.

p2.text: An accusation of favoritism forces the judges to disclose their criteria; the disputed result is upheld, reversed, or declared a tie.

p3.text: Competitors from both communities secretly practice together and publicly acknowledge each other when the results are announced.
